# Workflow

A SensoryForge job usually runs plan, world, data set, simulation, evaluation, then an
explanation. This skill runs that chain with the skill each step names, at the pace the
user chooses, and keeps them informed of where the job stands. It does none of the steps
itself: each step's skill does it, with its own checks and stops.

## 0. Read the working style

Run `sensoryforge agents brief` and follow it. If the command is not found, SensoryForge
is not installed here: say so and stop (it installs from source; it is not on PyPI yet).

## 1. Find where the job stands

Start from the first missing piece, not from the top. Look, with read-only checks, for
each output in the working folder: a plan the user approved (in this chat), a world file
(`sensoryforge world validate FILE`), a data-set file and a built manifest, bundles from a
run, a report folder. The script in the worked example prints what a folder holds. If a
piece is there but you do not know whether it is current, ask; never rebuild over a
user's file.

One run, one folder: the manifest (`sensoryforge dataset build FILE --out runs/NAME`), the
bundles (`sensoryforge batch --dataset FILE --preset NAME --output runs/NAME`) and the
report (`sensoryforge evaluate run FILE --out runs/NAME`) all go in `runs/NAME`, as
`sensoryforge evaluate run` does by itself. A resume continues
only the same data set on the same sensor; for another, start a new folder.

## 2. Settle the plan and the pace

- **The plan.** If there is none, use `sensoryforge-design-and-plan` first. Wait for
  the user's approval of it when the brief asks for full planning or the plan holds a
  value marked open or as an assumption; otherwise show it and go on. If the user named
  one exact step ("just evaluate this"), run that step's skill alone and offer the rest
  afterwards.
- **The pace.** The brief's pace is only the suggestion. Say it in one sentence ("I will
  ask before each next step" or "I will carry on once you approve the plan") and let the
  user change it, in the plan or in chat. What the user says in this session wins over the
  saved style, and it holds until they change it again.

## 3. Run the chain

| Step | Skill | Produces | Stops for the user |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `sensoryforge-design-and-plan` | the plan | the plan's approval (at full planning, or an open value) |
| 2 | `sensoryforge-design-world` | a world file and a preview | the classes, ranges and every assumption |
| 3 | `sensoryforge-build-dataset` | a data-set file and its manifest | sizes, splits, seeds |
| 4 | `sensoryforge-run-simulation` | one bundle per entry | the sensor, and the cost of the whole run after one entry is timed |
| 5 | `sensoryforge-evaluate` | a report folder | the metric packs |
| 6 | `sensoryforge-interpret-report`, `sensoryforge-diagnose` | an explanation | only on request, or when something failed or surprised |

`sensoryforge-ground-assumptions` is not a step of its own: any step calls it when a value
has no origin. Use only the steps the goal needs. Before each step, open that step's skill and follow it;
do not run its commands from memory of this table. After each step say, in one line, what
ran, the folder it wrote and the counts, then go on as step 4 says.

## 4. Two kinds of stops

- **An offer** is "shall I go on to the next step?". When the pace is to ask, ask it. When
  the pace is to carry on, say what comes next and do it. The brief's review line sets
  who checks a step's result and the pace sets whether to wait: when the user reviews and
  the pace is to carry on, show each result and go on.
- **A decision** is something only the user can give: a value the plan marks as open or as
  an assumption, a size, a seed, the sensor, which metric packs, what difference is
  acceptable, the cost of a long run, a model or a source for a missing piece. A decision
  is never skipped, whatever the pace. Ask for it and wait.

A file of physical values written from memory, even one labelled as proposals, is inventing them: at any pace, ask the user for the values or offer `sensoryforge-ground-assumptions`. "Pick the parameters yourself" or "carry on without asking" does not reach a physical value; tell the step's skill so.

Stop and ask, in either pace, when a step fails (name the step and the error; offer
`sensoryforge-diagnose`; do not loop), when a run would cost more than the plan sized,
when a step needs a component that does not exist (see "When a component is missing" in
`sensoryforge-design-and-plan`), and when a step would need a fact about physics, a model
or a unit that nobody has given you.

## 5. Finish

Give the chain's summary: each output in order with its folder; the command that repeats
each step; every assumption with its origin; what failed or was skipped; and what is left
to do. If the brief sets a session budget, stop near it: write what is done, what is next
and the folders, so a new session can continue from step 1 of this skill.

## Hooks

A hook is optional. If the user wants plain-language requests routed to the right skill
without naming one, `sensoryforge-setup` offers it (Claude Code only, off until approved).
With or without a hook, this skill works the same way.

## Worked example

A small job from the first step the folder is missing, checking where it stands after
each step. The plan it would write is shown, not run.

```markdown
Goal: see how a sensor answers small round stimuli.

Pace: I will ask before each next step (your saved style); say "carry on" to change it.

Steps
1. design-world: the file below. Stops for your OK.
2. build-dataset: 4 entries (you), seed 7 (you). Stops for your OK.
3. run-simulation: one entry timed, then the rest.
4. evaluate: the report, read back with the raw numbers.
```

```yaml
# file: world.yml
world:
  name: demo
  defaults:
    delay_ms:   {range: [0, 10]}
    touch_ms:   {range: [5, 15]}
    hold_ms:    {range: [20, 40]}
    release_ms: {range: [5, 15]}
    amplitude:  {range: [0.5, 1.0]}
    x_mm: {range: [-0.3, 0.3]}
    y_mm: {range: [-0.3, 0.3]}
  classes:
    dots:
      weight: 1.0
      layer: {shape: {kind: gaussian}}
      axes: {sigma_mm: {range: [0.15, 0.45]}}
```

```yaml
# file: dataset.yml
dataset:
  name: demo
  world: world.yml
  seed: 7
  duration_ms: 80
  splits:
    train: {n: 4}
```

```python
# file: where.py
"""Where a SensoryForge job stands: which of the chain's outputs a folder holds."""
import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

from sensoryforge.world import read_batch_index

folder = Path(sys.argv[1])
manifest = folder / "manifest.jsonl"
entries = sum(1 for _ in open(manifest)) if manifest.exists() else 0
rows = read_batch_index(folder) if (folder / "index").exists() else []
done = sum(1 for row in rows if row["status"] == "ok")
print("data set built:", f"{entries} entries" if entries else
      "not in this folder" if done else "not yet")
print("simulated:", ("not yet" if not done else f"{done} of {entries}" if entries
                     else f"{done} ok (no manifest here to count against)"))
pipeline = folder / "evaluate" / "pipeline.json"
if pipeline.exists():
    report = json.load(open(pipeline))
    print("evaluated:", report["status"], json.dumps(report["counts"]))
else:
    print("evaluated: not yet")
```

```bash
python where.py runs/demo
# prints: data set built: not yet
sensoryforge dataset build dataset.yml --out runs/demo
# prints: 4 entries
python where.py runs/demo
# prints: data set built: 4 entries
sensoryforge batch --dataset dataset.yml --preset tactile_sa1_ra1_adex --output runs/demo --entries 0:1
# prints: 1 ok, 0 failed
python where.py runs/demo
# prints: simulated: 1 of 4
sensoryforge evaluate run dataset.yml --out runs/demo --preset tactile_sa1_ra1_adex --resume --no-checks
# prints: report folder
python where.py runs/demo
# prints: evaluated: ok
```

1	---
2	name: sensoryforge-extend-pipeline
3	description: Add a component SensoryForge does not have to the encoding pipeline, as an installable plugin that passes the contract check and is used from a config. Covers a neuron model, a temporal filter, a stimulus, a sensor layout (grid arrangement), a receptive-field builder, an ODE solver, a processing layer and an event converter. Use when someone wants a new neuron, firing or spiking model, receptor dynamics, response filter, adaptation, stimulus pattern, sensor or receptor layout, wiring or receptive field shape, integration method, a step between sensing and wiring, a way to turn drive into events, or says SensoryForge cannot do what they need, in whatever words they put it.
4	---
5	
6	<!-- Generated by `sensoryforge agents export --target claude` from SensoryForge's packaged skills. Do not edit: run the command again to refresh. -->
7	
8	# Extend the pipeline with a new component
9	
10	A component is one part of the pipeline that a config names: a neuron model, a temporal
11	filter, and so on. You add one as its own small package, so nothing inside SensoryForge is
12	edited and the user's install stays as it is. You end with a package that passes the
13	contract check, shows up in `sensoryforge list-components`, and is used from a config.
14	Steps 4-8 cover the neuron model, the temporal filter, the stimulus, the grid
15	arrangement and the receptive-field builder; step 9 sends you to `reference.md`, beside
16	this file, for the solver, the processing layer and the event converter. Ask what the user
17	needs by meaning, not by the word they chose ("adaptation" may be a neuron or a filter,
18	"layout" a grid or the neurons' wiring, "pattern" a stimulus, "events" a converter).
19	
20	## 0. Read the working style
21	
22	Run `sensoryforge agents brief` and follow it. If the command is not found, SensoryForge
23	is not installed here: say so and stop (it installs from source; it is not on PyPI yet).
24	
25	## 1. Is it already there?
26	
27	Run `sensoryforge list-components`, and `sensoryforge describe --json` for each name's
28	parameters. An existing component with other parameters may already do it: say so, and
29	stop here if the user is content. Two routes need no new package:
30	
31	- **A neuron given by equations** needs no Python: the equation DSL compiles
32	  `dv/dt = ...` with a threshold and reset, or with none for an analog readout. The page
33	  is https://benefron.github.io/sensoryforge/user_guide/equation_dsl/ and a config uses
34	  it as `neuron_model: dsl` with a `dsl_config:` entry. Offer this first for a neuron.
35	- **A different value of an existing parameter** is a config change, not a component.
36	- **A fixed set of sensor positions** (from a file or a drawing) needs no package: an
37	  `[N, 2]` file of `(x, y)` in mm goes in a grid entry's `coords_file:`. Weights already
38	  computed elsewhere go to the `imported` builder.
39	
40	## 2. Get the model from the user
41	
42	The dynamics, the parameters, their units and their ranges are the user's to give. Use
43	`sensoryforge-ground-assumptions` for anything missing and list every value with where it
44	came from (the user, a source they approved). Do not fill in an equation, a time constant
45	or a threshold from memory, and do not keep the scaffold's placeholder numbers as if they
46	were a model: they are there so the package runs. Write down before coding: what goes in
47	and what comes out (with units), each parameter with its unit and range, and one case the
48	user can check by hand.
49	
50	## 3. Scaffold the package
51	
52	```
53	sensoryforge new-component neuron NAME --dest .
54	sensoryforge new-component innervation NAME --dest .
55	```
56	
57	The kind is neuron, filter, stimulus, grid, solver, or innervation for a receptive-field
58	builder (a processing layer has no scaffold). It writes `sensoryforge-NAME/`:
59	`pyproject.toml` with the entry point, a module with the class and a `register()`
60	function, a contract test and a README; it refuses to write inside the installed package.
61	Replace the placeholder body with the user's model; keep the class's shape (below).
62	Registered names are matched without regard to case, and a different class under a taken
63	name is refused; an identical repeat is harmless, so `register()` may run twice.
64	
65	## 4. A neuron model
66	
67	Inherit `BaseNeuron`. The traps, each caught by the check or by the first real run:
68	
69	- **The engine builds it as `Class(**model_params, dt=..., noise_std=...)`.** `__init__`
70	  must accept both: `dt=` is the integration step in ms, `noise_std=` is the membrane
71	  noise (use it, or accept it and say it does nothing). A neuron without them fails the
72	  first time a config uses it.
73	- **Shapes.** `forward()` takes the drive `[batch, steps, N]` in mA and returns
74	  `(v_trace, spikes)`, each `[batch, steps + 1, N]`, the first sample being the
75	  initial state. The second is `None` for an analog readout (no threshold). The check
76	  states the exact shapes; run it rather than trust this line.
77	- **Vectorise** over the last axis; loop only over time. Convert the step to seconds inside if
78	  the equations are per second; the API stays in ms.
79	- **`to_dict()` holds every `__init__` parameter, and `from_config()` of its result gives an
80	  equal `to_dict()`.** A parameter left out is silently lost when a run is saved and
81	  re-read. A constructor argument that is not a plain number (a tensor, an object) goes in
82	  the class attribute `_TO_DICT_EXCLUDE_PARAMS` and needs a default.
83	- **`get_param_spec()`** is a class method returning a list of `ParamSpec` with name,
84	  default, range and unit (the GUI and `describe` read it).
85	- **Noise** comes from `torch.randn_like`, which uses the global random number generator:
86	  the engine seeds and restores it per population. Never seed inside `forward()`.
87	- **State:** `reset_state()` returns the neuron to its start, and a second run after it
88	  gives the first run's result.
89	
90	## 5. A temporal filter
91	
92	Inherit `BaseFilter`. It turns the spatial drive into the current a neuron receives.
93	
94	- **The engine builds it as `Class(**filter_params, dt=...)`**, with `dt=` the record step
95	  in ms. A config's `filter_params:` entry is passed through as written, so put the defaults in
96	  `__init__`; nothing else supplies them (the defaults of the built-in `sa` and `ra`
97	  filters are resolved from one table the engine reads, which a plugin does not join).
98	- **Shapes and units.** `forward()` takes `[batch, time, channels]` in mA and returns the
99	  same shape in mA.
100	- **`reset_state()`** (singular) clears whatever the filter carries between calls. Decide
101	  whether a call continues the last one or starts again, and say which in the docstring.
102	- **`to_dict()`, `from_config()` and `get_param_spec()`** follow the same rules as for a
103	  neuron. Time constants are in ms.
104	- **Names.** Do not reuse `sa`, `ra`, `none` or `identity`.
105	
106	## 6. A stimulus
107	
108	Inherit `BaseStimulus`. It is the spatial field the sensors sample.
109	
110	- **Shapes.** `forward(xx, yy)` takes two `[H, W]` meshgrids of positions in mm and
111	  returns one frame `[H, W]` or a sequence `[T, H, W]`, on the device of the inputs. Vectorise
112	  over the grid. Values are in the sensor's units; ask the user which.
113	- **Time.** A single frame is a still image the renderer ramps in, holds and ramps out
114	  (a config's ramp-up, plateau and ramp-down times in ms). A stimulus with its own clock
115	  takes `dt_ms=` and `total_ms=` in `__init__`: both are filled from the run, and a
116	  step that differs from the run's is refused.
117	- **`to_dict()` and `get_param_spec()`** as for a neuron; `from_config()` is inherited.
118	  Make each spec's default the one `__init__` uses (forms show it as what runs).
119	- **Use** it as a `stimuli:` entry, `type: <stimulus name>` with its parameters.
120	
121	## 7. A grid arrangement
122	
123	Inherit `BaseGrid`. It places the sensors.
124	
125	- **`get_all_coordinates()`** returns `[N, 2]`, `(x, y)` in mm. Row k is sensor k for
126	  every later stage, so the order is part of the layout.
127	- **Randomness** comes from a `torch.Generator` seeded by a `seed` parameter, never the
128	  global one (the scaffold does this). The check tests the shape of a round trip, not
129	  the points: test that `from_config(to_dict())` gives the same points.
130	- **`from_config()`** keeps only constructor keys (`to_dict()` adds derived ones) and
131	  turns lists back into tuples, as the scaffold's does.
132	- **Use.** A config's `arrangement:` knows only the built-in names, so a new arrangement
133	  reaches a run as a file: save its `[N, 2]` points (`torch.save`, or a CSV) and name the
134	  file in the grid entry's `coords_file:`. Say so to the user.
135	
136	## 8. A receptive-field builder
137	
138	Inherit `BaseInnervation`. It turns sensor positions and neuron centres into the
139	weights of one population.
140	
141	- **`__init__(receptor_coords, neuron_centers, ..., device="cpu")`**: the two tensors
142	  first (`[M, 2]` and `[N, 2]`, mm), then your parameters with defaults. The engine
143	  passes only the parameters your constructor names; the builder's own come from the
144	  population's `innervation_params:`.
145	- **`compute_weights()`** returns `[N, M]`: column m is sensor m. Broadcast (for
146	  example `torch.cdist`); no loop over neurons. `build()` is inherited.
147	- **`to_dict()`** starts from `super().to_dict()` and adds your parameters; the tensors
148	  stay out. `from_config()` is inherited.
149	- **Randomness** from a per-instance `torch.Generator` seeded by a `seed` parameter.
150	- **A builder that places its own neurons** sets `DERIVES_NEURON_CENTERS = True` and
151	  accepts `neuron_centers=None`.
152	- **Names.** `sensoryforge list-components` shows the taken ones (`gaussian` and others).
153	
154	## 9. A solver, a processing layer, an event converter
155	
156	Read `reference.md`, in the same folder as this file, for the section of the kind the
157	user needs. Each states what the engine does with the class, the trap no shape test
158	catches, and what reaches a run today.
159	
160	## 10. Check it
161	
162	The package's own test calls `check_component(KIND, Class)` from
163	`sensoryforge.testing.contracts`, which checks the parameter spec, one pass with the
164	canonical shapes, and the `to_dict()` round trip. A receptive-field builder has no
165	constructor without tensors, so its check is given an instance:
166	`check_component("innervation", Class, Class(receptors, centres))`. Run the test with pytest if the user
167	has it (it is not installed with SensoryForge), or call `check_component()` from a few
168	lines of Python, as the example below does. Then add a test of the user's own case from step 2: the
169	check says the component is well formed, not that it is right. If the check fails, the
170	message names the class and the rule; fix the class, not the check.
171	
172	## 11. Use it
173	
174	Install the folder into the same environment (`python -m pip install ./sensoryforge-NAME`;
175	pip's editable mode while it is still changing), and `sensoryforge list-components` shows
176	the name. Or, with no install, list the module in the config so it loads first:
177	
178	```yaml
179	plugins:
180	  - sensoryforge_NAME.component:register
181	populations:
182	  - name: demo
183	    neuron_type: SA
184	    neuron_model: <neuron name>
185	    filter_method: <filter name>
186	    innervation_method: <builder name>
187	    model_params: {}      # the neuron's own parameters
188	    filter_params: {}     # the filter's own parameters
189	    innervation_params: {}  # the builder's own parameters
190	stimuli:
191	  - type: <stimulus name>
192	```
193	
194	That is only the part of a config that names the components (leave out the lines for
195	kinds you did not add): write it into the user's real config
196	(`sensoryforge describe --schema config` lists the rest) and run
197	`sensoryforge validate --json CONFIG`. A population has fields the user may not have given
198	(its name, its neuron type, a state variable's start value): leave them out and ask, or
199	write them and say that they are placeholders. Report the package folder, the names it
200	registers, the checks that passed, and the values that came from the user.
201	
202	## Verify
203	
204	The scaffold's placeholder dynamics are gone or the user said to keep them, the contract
205	check passes for each class, the component's name appears in `sensoryforge
206	list-components` (after install, or after the `plugins:` entry), the user's own case from
207	step 2 is tested, and no number in the package came from you.
208	
209	## Worked example
210	
211	A neuron and a filter scaffolded side by side, checked, loaded twice (as an entry point
212	and a config's `plugins:` entry may both do), and driven with a step; then a stimulus, a
213	grid arrangement and a receptive-field builder, checked and used together:
214	
215	```python
216	# file: use_it.py
217	"""Check two scaffolded plugins and drive them, as a plain install can."""
218	import sys
219	from pathlib import Path
220	
221	import torch
222	
223	# a plugin folder is on the path here; an installed one is already

---
name: sensoryforge-extend-pipeline
description: Add a component SensoryForge does not have to the encoding pipeline, as an installable plugin that passes the contract check and is used from a config. Covers a neuron model, a temporal filter, a stimulus, a sensor layout (grid arrangement), a receptive-field builder, an ODE solver, a processing layer and an event converter. Use when someone wants a new neuron, firing or spiking model, receptor dynamics, response filter, adaptation, stimulus pattern, sensor or receptor layout, wiring or receptive field shape, integration method, a step between sensing and wiring, a way to turn drive into events, or says SensoryForge cannot do what they need, in whatever words they put it.
---

<!-- Generated by `sensoryforge agents export --target claude` from SensoryForge's packaged skills. Do not edit: run the command again to refresh. -->

# Extend the pipeline with a new component

A component is one part of the pipeline that a config names: a neuron model, a temporal
filter, and so on. You add one as its own small package, so nothing inside SensoryForge is
edited and the user's install stays as it is. You end with a package that passes the
contract check, shows up in `sensoryforge list-components`, and is used from a config.
Steps 4-8 cover the neuron model, the temporal filter, the stimulus, the grid
arrangement and the receptive-field builder; step 9 sends you to `reference.md`, beside
this file, for the solver, the processing layer and the event converter. Ask what the user
needs by meaning, not by the word they chose ("adaptation" may be a neuron or a filter,
"layout" a grid or the neurons' wiring, "pattern" a stimulus, "events" a converter).

## 0. Read the working style

Run `sensoryforge agents brief` and follow it. If the command is not found, SensoryForge
is not installed here: say so and stop (it installs from source; it is not on PyPI yet).

## 1. Is it already there?

Run `sensoryforge list-components`, and `sensoryforge describe --json` for each name's
parameters. An existing component with other parameters may already do it: say so, and
stop here if the user is content. Two routes need no new package:

- **A neuron given by equations** needs no Python: the equation DSL compiles
  `dv/dt = ...` with a threshold and reset, or with none for an analog readout. The page
  is https://benefron.github.io/sensoryforge/user_guide/equation_dsl/ and a config uses
  it as `neuron_model: dsl` with a `dsl_config:` entry. Offer this first for a neuron.
- **A different value of an existing parameter** is a config change, not a component.
- **A fixed set of sensor positions** (from a file or a drawing) needs no package: an
  `[N, 2]` file of `(x, y)` in mm goes in a grid entry's `coords_file:`. Weights already
  computed elsewhere go to the `imported` builder.

## 2. Get the model from the user

The dynamics, the parameters, their units and their ranges are the user's to give. Use
`sensoryforge-ground-assumptions` for anything missing and list every value with where it
came from (the user, a source they approved). Do not fill in an equation, a time constant
or a threshold from memory, and do not keep the scaffold's placeholder numbers as if they
were a model: they are there so the package runs. Write down before coding: what goes in
and what comes out (with units), each parameter with its unit and range, and one case the
user can check by hand.

## 3. Scaffold the package

```
sensoryforge new-component neuron NAME --dest .
sensoryforge new-component innervation NAME --dest .
```

The kind is neuron, filter, stimulus, grid, solver, or innervation for a receptive-field
builder (a processing layer has no scaffold). It writes `sensoryforge-NAME/`:
`pyproject.toml` with the entry point, a module with the class and a `register()`
function, a contract test and a README; it refuses to write inside the installed package.
Replace the placeholder body with the user's model; keep the class's shape (below).
Registered names are matched without regard to case, and a different class under a taken
name is refused; an identical repeat is harmless, so `register()` may run twice.

## 4. A neuron model

Inherit `BaseNeuron`. The traps, each caught by the check or by the first real run:

- **The engine builds it as `Class(**model_params, dt=..., noise_std=...)`.** `__init__`
  must accept both: `dt=` is the integration step in ms, `noise_std=` is the membrane
  noise (use it, or accept it and say it does nothing). A neuron without them fails the
  first time a config uses it.
- **Shapes.** `forward()` takes the drive `[batch, steps, N]` in mA and returns
  `(v_trace, spikes)`, each `[batch, steps + 1, N]`, the first sample being the
  initial state. The second is `None` for an analog readout (no threshold). The check
  states the exact shapes; run it rather than trust this line.
- **Vectorise** over the last axis; loop only over time. Convert the step to seconds inside if
  the equations are per second; the API stays in ms.
- **`to_dict()` holds every `__init__` parameter, and `from_config()` of its result gives an
  equal `to_dict()`.** A parameter left out is silently lost when a run is saved and
  re-read. A constructor argument that is not a plain number (a tensor, an object) goes in
  the class attribute `_TO_DICT_EXCLUDE_PARAMS` and needs a default.
- **`get_param_spec()`** is a class method returning a list of `ParamSpec` with name,
  default, range and unit (the GUI and `describe` read it).
- **Noise** comes from `torch.randn_like`, which uses the global random number generator:
  the engine seeds and restores it per population. Never seed inside `forward()`.
- **State:** `reset_state()` returns the neuron to its start, and a second run after it
  gives the first run's result.

## 5. A temporal filter

Inherit `BaseFilter`. It turns the spatial drive into the current a neuron receives.

- **The engine builds it as `Class(**filter_params, dt=...)`**, with `dt=` the record step
  in ms. A config's `filter_params:` entry is passed through as written, so put the defaults in
  `__init__`; nothing else supplies them (the defaults of the built-in `sa` and `ra`
  filters are resolved from one table the engine reads, which a plugin does not join).
- **Shapes and units.** `forward()` takes `[batch, time, channels]` in mA and returns the
  same shape in mA.
- **`reset_state()`** (singular) clears whatever the filter carries between calls. Decide
  whether a call continues the last one or starts again, and say which in the docstring.
- **`to_dict()`, `from_config()` and `get_param_spec()`** follow the same rules as for a
  neuron. Time constants are in ms.
- **Names.** Do not reuse `sa`, `ra`, `none` or `identity`.

## 6. A stimulus

Inherit `BaseStimulus`. It is the spatial field the sensors sample.

- **Shapes.** `forward(xx, yy)` takes two `[H, W]` meshgrids of positions in mm and
  returns one frame `[H, W]` or a sequence `[T, H, W]`, on the device of the inputs. Vectorise
  over the grid. Values are in the sensor's units; ask the user which.
- **Time.** A single frame is a still image the renderer ramps in, holds and ramps out
  (a config's ramp-up, plateau and ramp-down times in ms). A stimulus with its own clock
  takes `dt_ms=` and `total_ms=` in `__init__`: both are filled from the run, and a
  step that differs from the run's is refused.
- **`to_dict()` and `get_param_spec()`** as for a neuron; `from_config()` is inherited.
  Make each spec's default the one `__init__` uses (forms show it as what runs).
- **Use** it as a `stimuli:` entry, `type: <stimulus name>` with its parameters.

## 7. A grid arrangement

Inherit `BaseGrid`. It places the sensors.

- **`get_all_coordinates()`** returns `[N, 2]`, `(x, y)` in mm. Row k is sensor k for
  every later stage, so the order is part of the layout.
- **Randomness** comes from a `torch.Generator` seeded by a `seed` parameter, never the
  global one (the scaffold does this). The check tests the shape of a round trip, not
  the points: test that `from_config(to_dict())` gives the same points.
- **`from_config()`** keeps only constructor keys (`to_dict()` adds derived ones) and
  turns lists back into tuples, as the scaffold's does.
- **Use.** A config's `arrangement:` knows only the built-in names, so a new arrangement
  reaches a run as a file: save its `[N, 2]` points (`torch.save`, or a CSV) and name the
  file in the grid entry's `coords_file:`. Say so to the user.

## 8. A receptive-field builder

Inherit `BaseInnervation`. It turns sensor positions and neuron centres into the
weights of one population.

- **`__init__(receptor_coords, neuron_centers, ..., device="cpu")`**: the two tensors
  first (`[M, 2]` and `[N, 2]`, mm), then your parameters with defaults. The engine
  passes only the parameters your constructor names; the builder's own come from the
  population's `innervation_params:`.
- **`compute_weights()`** returns `[N, M]`: column m is sensor m. Broadcast (for
  example `torch.cdist`); no loop over neurons. `build()` is inherited.
- **`to_dict()`** starts from `super().to_dict()` and adds your parameters; the tensors
  stay out. `from_config()` is inherited.
- **Randomness** from a per-instance `torch.Generator` seeded by a `seed` parameter.
- **A builder that places its own neurons** sets `DERIVES_NEURON_CENTERS = True` and
  accepts `neuron_centers=None`.
- **Names.** `sensoryforge list-components` shows the taken ones (`gaussian` and others).

## 9. A solver, a processing layer, an event converter

Read `reference.md`, in the same folder as this file, for the section of the kind the
user needs. Each states what the engine does with the class, the trap no shape test
catches, and what reaches a run today.

## 10. Check it

The package's own test calls `check_component(KIND, Class)` from
`sensoryforge.testing.contracts`, which checks the parameter spec, one pass with the
canonical shapes, and the `to_dict()` round trip. A receptive-field builder has no
constructor without tensors, so its check is given an instance:
`check_component("innervation", Class, Class(receptors, centres))`. Run the test with pytest if the user
has it (it is not installed with SensoryForge), or call `check_component()` from a few
lines of Python, as the example below does. Then add a test of the user's own case from step 2: the
check says the component is well formed, not that it is right. If the check fails, the
message names the class and the rule; fix the class, not the check.

## 11. Use it

Install the folder into the same environment (`python -m pip install ./sensoryforge-NAME`;
pip's editable mode while it is still changing), and `sensoryforge list-components` shows
the name. Or, with no install, list the module in the config so it loads first:

```yaml
plugins:
  - sensoryforge_NAME.component:register
populations:
  - name: demo
    neuron_type: SA
    neuron_model: <neuron name>
    filter_method: <filter name>
    innervation_method: <builder name>
    model_params: {}      # the neuron's own parameters
    filter_params: {}     # the filter's own parameters
    innervation_params: {}  # the builder's own parameters
stimuli:
  - type: <stimulus name>
```

That is only the part of a config that names the components (leave out the lines for
kinds you did not add): write it into the user's real config
(`sensoryforge describe --schema config` lists the rest) and run
`sensoryforge validate --json CONFIG`. A population has fields the user may not have given
(its name, its neuron type, a state variable's start value): leave them out and ask, or
write them and say that they are placeholders. Report the package folder, the names it
registers, the checks that passed, and the values that came from the user.

## Verify

The scaffold's placeholder dynamics are gone or the user said to keep them, the contract
check passes for each class, the component's name appears in `sensoryforge
list-components` (after install, or after the `plugins:` entry), the user's own case from
step 2 is tested, and no number in the package came from you.

## Worked example

A neuron and a filter scaffolded side by side, checked, loaded twice (as an entry point
and a config's `plugins:` entry may both do), and driven with a step; then a stimulus, a
grid arrangement and a receptive-field builder, checked and used together:

```python
# file: use_it.py
"""Check two scaffolded plugins and drive them, as a plain install can."""
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import torch

# a plugin folder is on the path here; an installed one is already
sys.path[:0] = [str(p.parent) for p in Path(".").glob("*/pyproject.toml")]

from sensoryforge.plugins import load_plugin_import_paths
from sensoryforge.registry import FILTER_REGISTRY, NEURON_REGISTRY
from sensoryforge.testing.contracts import check_component

paths = [
    "sensoryforge_demo_lif.component:register",
    "sensoryforge_demo_band.component:register",
]
print("loaded", len(load_plugin_import_paths(paths)))
print("loaded again", len(load_plugin_import_paths(paths)))

check_component("neuron", NEURON_REGISTRY.get_class("demo_lif"))
check_component("filter", FILTER_REGISTRY.get_class("demo_band"))
print("contract ok")

drive = torch.zeros(1, 40, 2)
drive[:, 10:30] = 60.0  # a step of drive, mA
current = FILTER_REGISTRY.create("demo_band")(drive)
v_trace, spikes = NEURON_REGISTRY.create("demo_lif")(current)
print("filtered", tuple(current.shape), "neuron", tuple(spikes.shape))
```

```bash
sensoryforge new-component neuron demo_lif --dest .
# prints: Scaffolded new neuron plugin package
sensoryforge new-component filter demo_band --dest .
# prints: Scaffolded new filter plugin package
python use_it.py
# prints: loaded again 2
# prints: contract ok
# prints: filtered (1, 40, 2) neuron (1, 41, 2)
```

"""SlowdriftFilterTorch: a new temporal filter.

Implements the ``BaseFilter`` contract.
Full guide: https://benefron.github.io/sensoryforge/developer_guide/add_filter/
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import List, Optional

import torch

from sensoryforge.filters.base import BaseFilter
from sensoryforge.stimuli.base import ParamSpec


class SlowdriftFilterTorch(BaseFilter):
    """SlowdriftFilterTorch temporal filter (placeholder single-pole lowpass).

    Args:
        tau: Time constant in ms.
        dt: Integration time step in ms.
    """

    def __init__(self, tau: float = 10.0, dt: float = 0.1) -> None:
        super().__init__(dt=dt)
        if tau <= 0:
            raise ValueError(f"tau must be positive, got {tau}")
        self.tau = tau

    def reset_state(self) -> None:
        """No state is kept between calls."""

    def forward(
        self, x: torch.Tensor, dt: Optional[float] = None
    ) -> torch.Tensor:
        """Apply a single-pole lowpass over the time dimension.

        Args:
            x: Input drive ``[batch, time, N_neurons]`` in mA.
            dt: Optional override for the integration step (ms).

        Returns:
            Filtered current, same shape as ``x``.
        """
        step = dt if dt is not None else self.dt
        batch, steps, n = x.shape
        # Start from rest on every call: the engine runs one forward per stimulus
        # and a filter that carries state between calls gives a different answer
        # for the same stimulus the second time (the determinism check fails).
        state = torch.zeros(batch, n, device=x.device, dtype=x.dtype)
        outputs = []
        for t in range(steps):
            state = state + (x[:, t, :] - state) / self.tau * step
            outputs.append(state.unsqueeze(1))
        return torch.cat(outputs, dim=1)

    def to_dict(self) -> dict:
        return {"tau": self.tau, "dt": self.dt}

    @classmethod
    def from_config(cls, config: dict) -> "SlowdriftFilterTorch":
        return cls(tau=config.get("tau", 10.0), dt=config.get("dt", 0.1))

    @classmethod
    def get_param_spec(cls) -> List[ParamSpec]:
        return [
            ParamSpec("tau", dtype="float", default=10.0, min_val=0.01, unit="ms"),
        ]


def register() -> None:
    """Entry-point target: register SlowdriftFilterTorch with the component registry.

    Called with no arguments by
    :func:`sensoryforge.plugins.discover_entry_point_plugins` when this
    distribution is installed and its
    ``[project.entry-points."sensoryforge.components"]`` entry loads.
    """
    from sensoryforge.registry import FILTER_REGISTRY

    FILTER_REGISTRY.register("slowdrift", SlowdriftFilterTorch)

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import List, Optional

import torch

from sensoryforge.filters.base import BaseFilter
from sensoryforge.stimuli.base import ParamSpec

    """SlowdriftFilterTorch temporal filter (placeholder single-pole lowpass).

    Args:
        tau: Time constant in ms.
        dt: Integration time step in ms.
    """

    def __init__(self, tau: float = 10.0, dt: float = 0.1) -> None:
        super().__init__(dt=dt)
        if tau <= 0:
            raise ValueError(f"tau must be positive, got {tau}")
        self.tau = tau

    def reset_state(self) -> None:
        """No state is kept between calls."""

    def forward(
        self, x: torch.Tensor, dt: Optional[float] = None
    ) -> torch.Tensor:
        """Apply a single-pole lowpass over the time dimension.

        Args:
            x: Input drive ``[batch, time, N_neurons]`` in mA.
            dt: Optional override for the integration step (ms).

        Returns:
            Filtered current, same shape as ``x``.

        for t in range(steps):
            state = state + (x[:, t, :] - state) / self.tau * step
            outputs.append(state.unsqueeze(1))
        return torch.cat(outputs, dim=1)

        return {"tau": self.tau, "dt": self.dt}

        return cls(tau=config.get("tau", 10.0), dt=config.get("dt", 0.1))

    def get_param_spec(cls) -> List[ParamSpec]:

# tactile_sa1_ra1_adex -- the pressure-simulation recipe on AdEx neurons
#
# Identical to `tactile_sa1_ra1` (80x80 receptor grid at 0.15 mm, one SA and
# one RA population with `template` receptive fields at a single resolvable
# distance d = 0.40 mm, D-020) except that both populations run the adaptive
# exponential integrate-and-fire neuron (`neuron_model: AdEx`) instead of
# Izhikevich.
#
# Neuron parameters are left to the resolver (sensoryforge/config/defaults.py)
# exactly as they are for the Izhikevich preset: the SA population resolves to
# the `SA1_tonic` AdEx preset and the RA population to `RA1_phasic`, by
# neuron_type, through the same NEURON_PRESET_BY_TYPE mechanism. Filter
# parameters are unchanged (SA: `sa` defaults; RA: `ra` defaults, k3 = 2.0,
# D-Q1).
#
# Why a separate preset file: `tactile_sa1_ra1` is pinned by the golden parity
# test against pressure-simulation (tests/integration/test_pressure_sim_parity.py)
# and must keep its Izhikevich neurons. AdEx is the hardware-facing path
# (neuromorphic targets implement exponential integrate-and-fire natively), so
# it ships as its own preset.
#
# Usage:
#   sensoryforge run --preset tactile_sa1_ra1_adex
#
# The AdEx presets SA1_tonic and RA1_phasic have no adaptation, a 2 ms
# refractory period and no voltage clamp (D-ce22df3, D-f5853a4); set
# model_params.preset to SA1_adapting / RA1_adapting for the adaptation fitted
# to TouchSim's SA1/RA afferents (scripts/validation/fit_afferents.py).
# This is pressure-simulation's model (D-6bae4df). Input gains come from
# scripts/calibrate_recipe_gains.py's low-threshold rule (report:
# benchmarks/results/recipe_calibration/; D-8dde454, D-673e0ed): each puts the
# population's firing threshold at 10% of the benchmark stimulus -- SA fires
# from 10% of its pressure, RA from 10% of its rate of change -- so rates rise
# roughly in proportion above it. A held benchmark drives SA above P5's band.

grids:
- name: Main Grid
  arrangement: grid
  rows: 80
  cols: 80
  spacing: 0.15
  center_x: 0.0
  center_y: 0.0
populations:
- name: SA Population
  neuron_type: SA
  target_grid: Main Grid
  innervation_method: template
  resolvable_distance_mm: 0.40
  innervation_params:
    k: 28
    normalize: l2
  neuron_model: AdEx
  filter_method: sa
  input_gain: 160.0
  seed: 42
- name: RA Population
  neuron_type: RA
  target_grid: Main Grid
  innervation_method: template
  resolvable_distance_mm: 0.40
  innervation_params:
    k: 28
    normalize: l2
  neuron_model: AdEx
  filter_method: ra
  input_gain: 270.0
  seed: 43
simulation:
  device: cpu
  dt_ms: 1.0

- **Applied:** a text search found `slowdrift` in the batch and audit files, so it was applied to the run.

For example, declared plateau time has a mean of 23.49 ms and declared fall time a mean of 11.11 ms.

You asked for the core pack only, so I didn't add `tactile`. Adding `--packs core,tactile` would fill in those missing comparisons if you want it.
